AudiomothR

R package to process the cards of AudioMoth recorders, from the SD card to the records of a citizen-science platform:

  1. Read the card: configuration (CONFIG.TXT), location and metadata of each WAV file (start time in UTC, battery, temperature), with checks of faulty, duplicated or triggered recordings. Optionally, copy the card to the disk first and work on the copy (the card can then be formatted).
  2. Analyse the recordings with BirdNET through birdnetR, with the species expected at the site and week (location filter) or an own list of species (that of BirdNET-Analyzer, a CSV file, or one built from the observations published in GBIF around the recorder), and a cache that resumes interrupted analyses.
  3. Review the species and extract examples: the exact sound of the best detections, their spectrogram and a video of the spectrogram with the audio.
  4. Validate the records by ear (optional) on a web page that works in any browser, from the least to the most plausible.
  5. Export to Observation.org, translating BirdNET names into the names of Observation.org.
  6. Create a PDF report of one or several recorders.

Who is it for? Ecologists, naturalists, technicians of protected areas and citizen-science volunteers who deploy AudioMoth recorders to monitor birds and want to go from the SD card to checked records without programming the workflow themselves. Basic knowledge of R is enough: each step is one function, the vignettes start from zero with an example card, and process_audiomoth() runs everything in one call. Bioacousticians can use it to organise many cards and boxes, choose the species that BirdNET looks for, and validate the detections by ear before publishing them.

New to AudiomothR? Everything, vignettes included, can be read on the web site of the package: https://ajcanepa.github.io/AudiomothR/. Follow the three vignettes in order, with the example card of the package: vignette("audiomothr-1-workflow") (the complete workflow), vignette("audiomothr-2-species") (which species BirdNET looks for) and vignette("audiomothr-3-boxes") (several cards, boxes and reports). See section 15.

1. Requirements

What Required What for How to install
R ≥ 4.1 Yes — https://cran.r-project.org
R packages birdnetR, tuneR, processx, cli, reticulate, rlang, jsonlite Yes BirdNET, audio, external programs, messages Installed with AudiomothR
ffmpeg Yes Converting audio to 48 kHz, clips and MP4 videos Linux: sudo apt install ffmpeg · macOS: brew install ffmpeg · Windows: winget install ffmpeg
Internet connection (first time only) Yes birdnetR downloads its Python, TensorFlow and the BirdNET model Automatic: Python does not need to be installed by hand
Internet connection (later) No Only for gbif_species_list() (species observed around the site, from GBIF) and the map of the report —
~3 GB of disk Yes Python environment of BirdNET (Python 3.11 and TensorFlow 2.15, in the reticulate/uv cache) and the model (73 MB) Automatic with setup_birdnet() (or the first analyze_birdnet())
seewave No Spectrogram computation (AudiomothR has an equivalent one of its own) install.packages("seewave")
rstudioapi or tcltk No Dialog to choose the card folder Come with RStudio / R
Quarto ≥ 1.4, knitr, rmarkdown No PDF report (create_report()); no LaTeX needed Included in RStudio and Positron; otherwise https://quarto.org
maptiles, sf, terra No Map of the recorders on OpenStreetMap in the report (without them, a map without background) install.packages(c("maptiles", "sf", "terra"))
testthat No Tests install.packages("testthat")

2. Installation 

install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("ajcanepa/AudiomothR")            # latest version
remotes::install_github("ajcanepa/AudiomothR@v0.4.0")     # a given version
# With the vignettes, to read them with browseVignettes("AudiomothR"):
remotes::install_github("ajcanepa/AudiomothR", build_vignettes = TRUE)

Building the vignettes needs knitr, rmarkdown and pandoc (pandoc comes with RStudio and Positron; in a plain R console, install it from https://pandoc.org). If the installation with vignettes fails, install without them: they can be read on the web site of the package, https://ajcanepa.github.io/AudiomothR/articles/.

Check that everything is ready:

library(AudiomothR)
check_requirements()   # what is installed, what is missing, language of the names
setup_birdnet()        # the 1st time: installs Python, TensorFlow and the BirdNET model (a few minutes)

setup_birdnet() works the same on Windows, macOS (Intel and Apple silicon) and Linux: birdnetR installs its own Python with uv, so neither Python nor TensorFlow have to be installed by hand, and AudiomothR downloads the BirdNET model itself (with retries and an integrity check) into the folder where BirdNET looks for it:

System Model folder
Windows %APPDATA%\birdnet\models\v2.4\TFLite
macOS ~/Library/Application Support/birdnet/models/v2.4/TFLite
Linux ~/.local/share/birdnet/models/v2.4/TFLite

Besides R, only ffmpeg has to be installed (see the table above) and, for the report, Quarto. On Windows, TensorFlow needs the Microsoft Visual C++ Redistributable, which almost every computer already has; if loading BirdNET fails with a message about msvcp140.dll, install it from https://aka.ms/vs/17/release/vc_redist.x64.exe.

3. Quick start (everything in one call) 

library(AudiomothR)

am <- process_audiomoth(
  folder = "/path/to/the/card",                   # or without it: a dialog opens
  coordinates = "41°07'24.4\"N 3°07'24.4\"W",     # copied from Google Earth
  site = "River - bridge",                        # optional
  output = "~/AudiomothR_results/box_01",          # one folder per box (all its cards)
  copy_to = TRUE,                                 # copy the card first and work on the copy
  example_species = "auto",                       # examples of the detected species
  validation = TRUE,                              # page to validate the records by ear
  report = TRUE                                   # PDF report (needs Quarto)
)

The folder is the root of the card: the one that contains CONFIG.TXT and the daily folders (20261006/, 20261007/…). The output folder keeps the results of the box: every new card of the same box is added to it (see “Several cards of the same box” below). When it is not given, it is asked for in the console, suggesting ~/AudiomothR_results/AudioMoth_<ID> (or the folder chosen before for the same box). With copy_to = TRUE the card is first copied into <output>/recordings/ and everything is done with the copy (see “Copying the card” below).

4. Step by step 

library(AudiomothR)

# 1. Card, CONFIG.TXT, location and inventory of the recordings (copying the
#    card to the disk first, recommended)
am <- read_audiomoth("/path/to/the/card", coordinates = "41.123456, -3.123456",
                     output = "~/AudiomothR_results/box_01", copy_to = TRUE)

# 2-3. Audio ready for BirdNET and analysis (it resumes if interrupted)
am <- prepare_audio(am)                 # optional: analyze_birdnet() does it
am <- analyze_birdnet(am)               # common names in the language of the system
am <- analyze_birdnet(am, language = "es")   # ...or in another one (no new analysis)
# ...or only the species of an own list, instead of the location filter
am <- analyze_birdnet(am, species_list = "~/species_list.txt")    # BirdNET-Analyzer list
am <- analyze_birdnet(am, species_list = gbif_species_list(am))   # observed around, in GBIF

# 4. Which species: prints a vector ready to copy, change the n and paste
species <- detected_species(am)
#> species <- c(
#>   "Cettia cetti"            = 3,  # Cetti's Warbler | 41 detections | confidence max. 0.97, mean 0.71
#>   "Troglodytes troglodytes" = 2,  # Eurasian Wren | 12 detections | ...
#> )

# 5. Examples (WAV + PNG + MP4) of the chosen species
extract_examples(am, species)                                   # the vector as returned
extract_examples(am, c("Cettia cetti" = 3, "Eurasian Wren" = 1))
extract_examples(am, "Cettia cetti", style = "scroll")           # another style of video

# 6. Validation by ear (optional): open the page, decide, download the decisions
create_validation(am)

# 7. CSV for Observation.org (applies the validation automatically)
export_observation(am)

# 8. PDF report (one recorder, or several: one section each or all together)
create_report(am)
create_report(list(am1, am2, am3), by_recorder = FALSE, output = "report_river")

Several cards of the same box

A box (AudioMoth) usually stays in the field for months while its SD cards are replaced every few days. Use one results folder per box: each card is read into it as a new deployment, with its own dates, site and location (the box may have been moved), and its recordings are added to those of the previous cards.

out <- "~/AudiomothR_results/box_01"
am <- read_audiomoth("/media/SD", coordinates = "41.123456, -3.123456",
                     site = "River - bridge", output = out)     # first card
am <- analyze_birdnet(am)
# ...ten days later, the next card (the box was moved to another site)
am <- read_audiomoth("/media/SD", coordinates = "41.300000, -3.400000",
                     site = "Pine forest", output = out)        # second card
am <- analyze_birdnet(am)          # only analyses the new recordings
export_observation(am)             # all the cards, each record with its location

The location of each card is the one given in coordinates or, otherwise, that of its CONFIG.TXT (with a warning: it must have been updated in the AudioMoth app when the box was moved). In an interactive session, if there is none, it is asked for (Enter = the site of the previous card). The cards are listed in AudioMoth_<ID>_deployments.csv; the results of a card that is no longer connected are kept, and the report shows every site on the map.

Copying the card (recommended)

By default the card is read where it is (it is never modified), and the steps that go back to the audio (examples, validation, a new analysis) need it connected. With copy_to the card is first copied to the disk and everything is done with the copy, so the card can be formatted for the next deployment:

read_audiomoth("/media/SD", output = out, copy_to = TRUE)              # <output>/recordings/<dates>/
read_audiomoth("/media/SD", output = out, copy_to = "/media/backup")   # /media/backup/AudioMoth_<ID>/<dates>/

The copy keeps the structure and dates of the card and checks the size of each file; an interrupted copy continues where it stopped. The original folder is kept in the column card_folder of AudioMoth_<ID>_deployments.csv.

Which species BirdNET looks for

By default, only the species that the BirdNET metadata model (trained with eBird checklists) expects at the site and week of each recording, with a probability of occurrence ≥ 0.03 (location_threshold). It works well for common species, but it may leave out species that are present yet seldom reported to eBird: nocturnal, secretive or scarce species, and little visited areas. Then:

Option Argument
Lower the threshold analyze_birdnet(am, location_threshold = 0.01)
Own list of species (vector, BirdNET-Analyzer .txt, CSV with a scientific_name column, data frame) analyze_birdnet(am, species_list = ...); check it with read_species_list(); template in system.file("extdata", "example", "species_list.csv", package = "AudiomothR")
Species observed around the site in GBIF (eBird, Observation.org, iNaturalist), without an account species_list = gbif_species_list(am, radius_km = 25)
No filter (more mistakes: validate by ear) analyze_birdnet(am, location_filter = FALSE)

Names of BirdNET, IOC, Observation.org or GBIF are accepted. The probability of occurrence is always kept in location_prob, and the validation page shows first the least plausible records. See vignette("audiomothr-2-species") for the details.

Resuming the work another day

Recordings already analysed are not analysed again: just repeat

am <- read_audiomoth("/path/to/the/card", coordinates = "41.123456, -3.123456",
                     output = "~/AudiomothR_results/box_01")
am <- analyze_birdnet(am)     # only analyses what is missing

The BirdNET cache (<output>/birdnet/) keeps one folder per combination of parameters: changing a parameter analyses the card again without deleting the previous results, and going back to the previous parameters reuses them. Changing language or raising min_confidence above 0.1 does not need a new analysis. If the location changes after the analysis (e.g. to correct it), export_observation() uses the current one.

5. Functions

Function What it does Returns
process_audiomoth() The whole workflow in one call audiomoth object
check_requirements() Which requirements (ffmpeg, birdnetR, Quarto…) are installed, how to install the missing ones and the language of the common names Logical vector
setup_birdnet() Installs and checks BirdNET (Python environment and model) TRUE
choose_folder() Dialog to choose the folder of the card Path
choose_output() Asks for the results folder in the console Path
read_audiomoth(folder, coordinates, site, precision_m, time_zone, output, copy_to) Reads CONFIG.TXT, the location and the metadata of all the WAV files (optionally copying the card to the disk first); saves the inventory audiomoth object (am$config, am$location, am$recordings)
read_config(file) Reads a CONFIG.TXT file List of settings
parse_coordinates(text) Reads coordinates copied from Google Earth / Maps or a GPS lat, lon, precision_m
prepare_audio(am) Converts to 48 kHz mono what needs it (expanding triggered recordings) am with birdnet_path
analyze_birdnet(am, min_confidence, language, version, location_filter, location_threshold, species_list, ...) Analyses with BirdNET (location filter or own list of species) and saves the CSV of detections am with am$detections
read_species_list(species_list) Reads a list of species (vector, BirdNET-Analyzer .txt, CSV, data frame) and translates it into BirdNET names Data frame
gbif_species_list(x, radius_km, months, years, datasets, min_records, file) Species observed in GBIF around the site (eBird, Observation.org, iNaturalist), in BirdNET names Data frame (usable as species_list)
read_detections(x) Reads the detections of an am or of an AudioMoth_<ID>_detections.csv Data frame
species_summary(x, min_confidence) Summary by species: detections, days, confidence, probability of occurrence, candidate examples Data frame
detected_species(x, min_confidence, example_confidence, n_max) Prints the detected species as a vector c("species" = n, ...) ready to paste into extract_examples(), and returns it Named vector
select_examples(x, species, n, ...) Chooses the best detections (without creating files) Data frame
extract_examples(am, species, n, margin_s, style, ...) Creates the WAV, PNG and MP4 of each example Index of examples
spectrogram_image(wav, file, ...) PNG spectrogram of any WAV file Path
spectrogram_video(wav, file, style, ...) MP4 video of the spectrogram of any WAV file, with its audio Path
create_validation(am, min_confidence, n_clips, ...) Web page to validate the records by ear Path of the page
read_validation(am, file) Reads the decisions of the validation Data frame
export_observation(am, min_confidence, min_detections, ...) Import CSV for Observation.org Data frame
create_report(recorders, by_recorder, output, ...) PDF report (Quarto + Typst) of one or several recorders Path of the PDF

The full help of each function is in R: ?analyze_birdnet, ?export_observation…

6. Location

AudioMoth only writes the location in CONFIG.TXT when it was set in its app, and with two decimals (~700 m). Therefore:

  1. If coordinates are given, they are used (with a warning if they are more than 10 km away from the CONFIG.TXT, and an error if latitude and longitude look swapped).
  2. Otherwise, the location of CONFIG.TXT is used (with a note about its low precision).
  3. If there is none either, it is asked for in the console in an interactive session (with a map link to check it); otherwise there is an error asking for coordinates.

coordinates accepts what is copied from Google Earth, Google Maps or a GPS:

Format Example
Decimal degrees (Google Maps / Earth) "41.123456, -3.123456"
Degrees, minutes and seconds "41°07'24.4\"N 3°07'24.4\"W"
Spanish hemisphere letters (O = west) "41°07'24.4\"N 3°07'24.4\"O"
Degrees and decimal minutes "41°07.407'N 3°07.407'W"
Hemisphere first (handheld GPS) "N41 07.407 W3 07.407"
Without symbols "41 07 24.4 N 3 07 24.4 W"
Google Earth placemark (KML) "<coordinates>-3.123456,41.123456,0</coordinates>"
Google Maps link "https://www.google.com/maps?q=41.123456,-3.123456"
Decimal comma "41,123456 -3,123456"
Numeric vector c(41.123456, -3.123456)

Without hemisphere letters the latitude goes first. The precision (column accuracy of Observation.org) follows from the decimals written; it can be set with read_audiomoth(precision_m = 10).

7. Times

AudioMoth records in UTC unless another zone was set in its app; the zone of each recording is read from its metadata. All local dates and times of the CSV files are in time_zone (by default Europe/Madrid, with daylight saving time; use "Atlantic/Canary" in the Canary Islands) and the column utc_offset keeps the offset of each one; recording_start_utc keeps the original UTC time.

8. Criteria

Step Criterion (default) Argument
Analysis Detections with confidence ≥ 0.10 are saved, only of the species expected at the site and week (BirdNET metadata model, threshold 0.03) or of an own list analyze_birdnet(min_confidence, location_filter, location_threshold, species_list)
Doubts A detection has no doubts when BirdNET proposed no other species in the same 3 s window with confidence ≥ 0.1 —
Examples Confidence ≥ 0.85 and no doubts; the ones with the highest confidence, at most one per recording extract_examples(min_confidence, no_doubts, n)
Validation Records (species and day) with detections of confidence ≥ 0.5, from the least to the most plausible create_validation(min_confidence, min_detections)
Observation.org One record per species and day; detections with confidence ≥ 0.80 and at least 2 that day, plus the records validated by ear export_observation(min_confidence, min_detections, no_doubts_only)

BirdNET gives a confidence score (0-1), not a measured precision: a high value does not guarantee that the identification is right.

9. Results

In the output folder (asked for when not given; better outside the card, which is usually formatted for the next deployment, and one per box: it gathers all the cards of the box):

File Contents
AudioMoth_<ID>_deployments.csv The cards (deployments) of the box: dates, site, location and its source, folder read and original card (card_folder)
recordings/<first date>-<last date>/ Copy of each card (only with copy_to = TRUE)
AudioMoth_<ID>_recordings.csv Inventory (all the cards): file, day, UTC and local time, duration, sample rate, battery, temperature, problems and state of the analysis
AudioMoth_<ID>_detections.csv All the detections: file, local date and time, start and end (s), species, confidence, n_labels_window, other_confidence_max, no_doubts, location_prob, coordinates
AudioMoth_<ID>_observation.csv / .json Import file for Observation.org and the criteria used
examples/<species>/*.wav, *.png, *.mp4 Clip, spectrogram and video of each example
examples/AudioMoth_<ID>_examples.csv Index of the examples (relative paths)
validation/ Validation page, clips and decisions (AudioMoth_<ID>_validation.csv)
report/ Quarto folder of the report (report.qmd, data and figures) and the PDF
birdnet/<ID>_<key>/ BirdNET results per recording, parameters, versions (metadata.txt), errors, probability of occurrence of the species and the own list of species used (species_list.csv); do not delete it
audio_48k/ 48 kHz mono copies (only when needed); they can be deleted once the analysis is finished
.inventory_cache.rds Metadata of the WAV files already read, so that reading the card again is fast

10. Observation.org

The CSV follows exactly the format of observations-import-example.xlsx (19 columns, UTF-8 without BOM, commas, dates YYYY-MM-DD, times HH:MM, decimal coordinates with a point), with these values:

Column Value
date / time Local date / time of the first detection of the day
scientific name Name of the bird species in Observation.org. BirdNET v2.4 labels (eBird/Clements) are translated into the IOC World Bird List v15.2 and then into the species list of Observation.org, which follows IOC with its own lumps and genera (e.g. Corvus cornix → Corvus corone, Saxicola stejnegeri → Saxicola maurus; the BirdNET name is kept in notes). Every bird of BirdNET v2.4 has a valid name of Observation.org (see inst/extdata/taxonomy/README.md). Classes that are not birds are left out; species split by IOC are translated according to the location when the rule is clear (e.g. Cecropis daurica → Cecropis rufula in Europe) and reported otherwise. Own equivalences with equivalences = c("BirdNET name" = "Observation.org name")
lat / lng / accuracy Location of the recorder and its precision (m, at most 1000)
number 1
notes "Identified with BirdNET <version>" ("ID mediante BirdNET <version>" in Spanish), whether it was validated by ear, and the best detection (file, second and confidence)
is certain True for the records validated by ear, False for the rest
method / counting method Oído / Sin especificar (values of the Observation.org import example)
external reference AudioMoth_<ID>_<YYYYMMDD>_<species>, unique and stable

method, counting_method and activity are checked against the values that Observation.org accepts for birds. If the CSV is edited by hand (e.g. with a spreadsheet, keeping it comma separated), a new export does not overwrite it.

11. Videos

spectrogram_video() draws the spectrogram once with R and ffmpeg animates it (about 1 s per video): MP4 H.264 + AAC, 1280×720, valid for any player and for social media.

  • style = "cursor": the whole spectrogram with a moving line.
  • style = "scroll": the spectrogram scrolls under a fixed line.

Dashed white lines mark the 3 s window of the detection. Other settings: fps, max_freq (Hz, 12 000 by default), db_range, width, height, window_s.

12. Approximate times

Measured on a 12-core laptop with 1-min recordings at 48 kHz:

Step Time
Inventory (read_audiomoth) ~2 s for 1,700 recordings
BirdNET (analyze_birdnet) ~1 s per 1-min recording (a card of 1,700 recordings: ~30 min)
Example (WAV + PNG + MP4) ~1 s
Validation page ~0.5 s per record
Observation.org seconds

Recordings at 250 kHz take longer (they are first converted to 48 kHz).

13. Troubleshooting

Message / symptom Solution
Cannot find ffmpeg Install ffmpeg (see Requirements) or set its path: options(AudiomothR.ffmpeg = "C:/ffmpeg/bin/ffmpeg.exe")
Cannot find Quarto Use RStudio or Positron (they include it), install it from https://quarto.org or set its path: options(AudiomothR.quarto = "/path/to/quarto")
The report needs Quarto 1.4 or later Update RStudio or Positron (they include Quarto), or install it from https://quarto.org
The report or the vignettes fail with namespace 'htmltools' ... is being loaded, but >= ... is required (or another package) An old package used by rmarkdown: install.packages(c("knitr", "rmarkdown", "htmltools", "xfun")) and restart R. check_requirements() shows the problem
Cannot write in ... The card is write-protected: give another output folder
The results folder ... already holds the results of another AudioMoth Use one output folder per box; each box gathers its own cards
The map of the report has no background Install maptiles, sf and terra, and check the Internet connection
There is no CONFIG.TXT Choose the root folder of the card, not a daily folder (or give coordinates to read a copy without CONFIG.TXT)
I cannot find the files (examples, spectrograms, videos, pages) They are in the results folder (am$output); the message of each function gives the full path. A folder in tempdir() is deleted when R closes
The validation page does not open in Firefox (“File not found”) on Ubuntu Firefox (and Chromium) installed as a snap cannot open files in /tmp: open the page in the Viewer of RStudio or in another browser, or use a results folder outside /tmp
The first run of BirdNET takes long Normal: it installs Python and TensorFlow and downloads the model once (run setup_birdnet() beforehand)
Cannot download the BirdNET v2.4 model Check the connection and run setup_birdnet() again, or download the zip shown in the message and unzip it into the model folder (see Installation)
Give the results folder with output In scripts (Rscript) the results folder must be given: output = "~/AudiomothR_results/box_01"
Species from other continents Check that location_filter = TRUE and that the coordinates are right (latitude first; west negative)
A species present at the site is never detected The location filter may leave it out (nocturnal, scarce species, little visited areas): lower location_threshold or use a species_list (see “Which species BirdNET looks for”)
... not species of BirdNET v2.4 and are ignored Names of the species list that BirdNET cannot detect (or typos); check the list with read_species_list()
GBIF does not answer gbif_species_list() needs an Internet connection; try again later
Examples or validation without audio after formatting the card Without copy_to, they need the card connected at the same path; read the cards with copy_to to keep a copy on the disk
0 of the 3 requested examples meet the criteria See species_summary() or lower min_confidence / use no_doubts = FALSE
A name “without a bird species in Observation.org” (only with own names) Add equivalences = c("BirdNET name" = "Observation.org name") in export_observation()
Messages options(AudiomothR.quiet = TRUE) hides the informative messages (warnings are always shown)

14. Origin of the code, data and licences

  • Reading of CONFIG.TXT and WAV files, and the first taxonomic equivalences, adapted from Biosonora. Export criteria and notes from the reports of the acoustic box (Informes_Quarto_Caja_Acustica).
  • AudiomothR: GPL (≥ 3). birdnetR: MIT. BirdNET models: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (non-commercial use only). IOC World Bird List: CC BY 3.0. See inst/COPYRIGHTS and inst/extdata/taxonomy/README.md; the taxonomy tables are rebuilt with data-raw/build_taxonomy.R.

15. Example data and vignettes

The package includes an example AudioMoth card in inst/extdata/example/card/ (system.file("extdata", "example", "card", package = "AudiomothR")): a CONFIG.TXT file and two days of real recordings (16 WAV files), anonymised: the device ID and the location are fictitious, and most WAV files were cut to 0.05 s (10 of the 16 appear with problem: "duration < 3 s", on purpose); 6 files keep ~7 s of real song. inst/extdata/example/birdnet_detections.csv has the detections that BirdNET v2.4 returned for this card, species_list.csv is a template of an own list of species, and gbif_species_list.csv is the list of the species observed in GBIF around the example site (made with gbif_species_list() on 2026-11-10).

Three vignettes, to be read in order, go through everything with this card:

  1. vignette("audiomothr-1-workflow"), Getting started: the complete workflow: installation and requirements, every step from the card to Observation.org and the PDF report, with what each one produces, the validation by ear and how to solve the usual problems.
  2. vignette("audiomothr-2-species"), Which species BirdNET looks for: the location filter, own lists of species (also those of BirdNET-Analyzer) and lists built from GBIF.
  3. vignette("audiomothr-3-boxes"), Several cards, several boxes and reports: the next cards of a box, a box that is moved, coming back another day and reports of several boxes.

With remotes::install_github("ajcanepa/AudiomothR", build_vignettes = TRUE) they can be read with browseVignettes("AudiomothR").

Before uploading the CSV to Observation.org, check it. BirdNET identifications are automatic and sometimes wrong: validate at least the unusual species or those with low confidence with create_validation().

16. Tests 

devtools::test()   # more than 350 checks; conversion, video and report tests are
                   # skipped without ffmpeg, without Quarto or on CRAN

BirdNET is replaced by a mock in the tests, so they run without Python.

17. How to cite

If you use AudiomothR, cite the version you used (citation("AudiomothR")):

Canepa-Oneto A, de la Fuente Gamero P, Barbero-Aparicio JA, Guerra Carande J, Fernández-Ruiz C, Olivares A, Marticorena-Sánchez R (2026). AudiomothR: Acoustic Processing of AudioMoth Recordings with BirdNET. R package version 0.4.0. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23646408

Each version published on GitHub is archived in Zenodo with its own DOI; the DOI above always resolves to the latest version.

Questions, problems and ideas are welcome as issues, in English or Spanish; see CONTRIBUTING for what to include and how to propose changes. Please note that the AudiomothR project is released with a Contributor Code of Conduct. By contributing to this project, you agree to abide by its terms.
